relationships.subject: C1-esterase inhibitor
relationships.evidence_quote: Plasma-derived C1-INH (pdC1-INH) products provide functional C1-INH to down-regulate FXIIa and plasma kallikrein activity, reducing bradykinin generation.

relationships.subject: icatibant
relationships.evidence_quote: Icatibant is a synthetic decapeptide and selective bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist administered subcutaneously.

relationships.subject: ecallantide
relationships.evidence_quote: Ecallantide is a recombinant protein that functions as a potent, selective, reversible inhibitor of plasma kallikrein.

relationships.subject: lanadelumab
relationships.evidence_quote: Lanadelumab is a fully human IgG1-Kappa monoclonal antibody that inhibits plasma kallikrein

relationships.subject: deucrictibant
relationships.evidence_quote: Deucrictibant is an investigational, small-molecule bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist

relationships.subject: C1-esterase inhibitor
relationships.evidence_quote: Most cases arise from C1-esterase inhibitor (C1-INH) deficiency (type 1) or dysfunction (type 2), leading to excess bradykinin generation

key_findings: HAE-C1-INH attacks arise from excess bradykinin; effective on-demand and prophylactic drugs target the contact system (C1-INH, kallikrein inhibitors, FXIIa inhibitor, B2 receptor antagonists).
Icatibant (B2 antagonist) cut median time to 50% symptom reduction vs placebo in FAST-3 (2.0 vs 19.8 h); access to modern therapies is uneven globally.
